events.title: The death of St. Augustine and the siege of Hippo
events.shortBlurb: The great bishop and Doctor died as the Vandals pressed their siege against his African city…
body: In 429 the Vandal king Genseric led his people from Spain into Roman Africa, and by the early summer of 430 his host stood before Hippo, where the defeated Count Boniface commanded the defense. Bishops driven from their sees crowded into the city, among them Possidius of Calama, Augustine's friend of forty years and his first biographer.

The siege held nearly fourteen months. In its third month Augustine fell mortally ill; he had the penitential psalms written out in large letters and hung on the walls about his bed, and for his last ten days would see no one but his physicians. He died on 28 August 430, in his seventy-sixth year, leaving no will, for he had nothing to leave but his books.

Hippo outlasted him by months before the Vandals took and burned it in 431; yet his library in the basilica escaped the flames, and his writings fed the West thereafter. His relics were later carried to Sardinia and thence to Pavia, and the Church of Roman Africa wasted under a century of Arian Vandal rule.
